The options for fine tuning the Discover Weekly have changed for the worse. Go back to genres.. The current trend of replacing precise controls with vague AI prompts like "make it more groovy" severely degrades the discovery experience. Music discovery requires concrete musical pillars like genre, instrumentation, and not subjective descriptors that the algorithm will interpret as it will. Users can already access AI text prompting across the app; forcing it into dedicated curation spaces strips away the tactile, surgical control over our music libraries. Reverting to explicit genre selections gives power back to the listener, ensuring Discover Weekly delivers targeted, fresh variety rather than an unpredictable black box of "vibes."

Managed young-listener accounts allow graphic spoken stories disguised as music. I created a Spotify managed account for a young listener specifically because Spotify describes it as a music-only experience without podcasts or audiobooks. However, my child can search terms such as scary stories and access spoken-word horror, true-crime and ghost stories that have been uploaded as music albums. One example is Mr. Nightmare. These are not songs; they are narrated stories about murders, crimes and frightening events, but Spotifys system treats them as music. Turning off explicit content does not solve the problem, and Spotify does not currently allow parents to block a genre, spoken-word recordings, search terms or categories. Parents must discover and block every individual artist manually, while new accounts and albums can continue appearing. Please add the following controls for managed young-listener accounts: Block all spoken-word content classified as music Block genres or content categories Block specified search terms Restrict listening to parent-approved artists or playlists Allow parents to report albums that appear to be incorrectly classified Apply meaningful age or content ratings to narrated material A music-only account should not provide unrestricted access to unrated true-crime and horror stories simply because they were uploaded under the music category
